question.prompt: Tell me about a time you mentored a junior engineer or helped a colleague level up their skills.
expectedPoints: Identifying specific technical or professional growth opportunities for the mentee
Structured pedagogical approach (pairing, code reviews with context, delegating ownership)
Fostering independence rather than providing quick answers
Tangible evidence of mentee development and reciprocal learnings for the mentor
commonMistakes: Describing simple code reviews without pedagogical depth
Doing the work for the mentee
No evidence of mentee's subsequent growth or self-sufficiency

transcript: Candidate: Last year, an associate engineer joined our team who was struggling with asynchronous programming and React hooks in TypeScript. During code reviews, I noticed they were frequently encountering stale closures and race conditions. Instead of just rewriting the code in their PRs, I set up a weekly 45-minute pairing session. We walked through the JavaScript event loop, built custom hooks together from scratch, and created a team guide on useEffect dependencies. Over the next three months, their PR rejection rate dropped significantly, and they independently designed and shipped our new search autocomplete component with zero major bugs. Helping them also forced me to clarify my own mental models of React internals.
notes: Well-articulated mentorship story. Shows patience, pedagogical pairing, concrete mentee milestone (search autocomplete), and reciprocal learning.
